name: Aldol Condensation & Cross Aldol
reactant: Aldehyde or Ketone possessing at least one α-hydrogen atom (e.g. 2 CH₃CHO)
reagent: Dilute aqueous alkali (dil. NaOH or Ba(OH)₂)
condition: Warm, followed by heating to eliminate water
mechanismType: Nucleophilic addition across carbonyl followed by E1cB dehydration
keyRule: Carbanion is formed at the α-carbon and attacks the second carbonyl carbon atom.

name: Cannizzaro Reaction
reactant: Aldehyde having NO α-hydrogen atom (e.g. HCHO, C₆H₅CHO)
product: Equimolar mixture of an alcohol and a carboxylate salt (self-redox disproportionation)
mechanismType: Hydride ion (:H⁻) transfer from one tetrahedral intermediate to another carbonyl
keyRule: In Cross Cannizzaro with Formaldehyde, Formaldehyde is ALWAYS oxidized to formic acid salt (HCOONa).

name: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) Reaction
reagent: X₂ (Cl₂ or Br₂) in presence of Red Phosphorus, followed by H₂O
mechanismType: In-situ acyl halide enol halogenation followed by hydrolysis
keyRule: Selective α-substitution; does not affect the -COOH carbonyl carbon directly.

name: Ozonolysis of Alkenes
reagent: 1. Ozone (O₃) in inert solvent (CH₂Cl₂), 2. Zn / H₂O (Reductive) or H₂O₂ (Oxidative)
product: Zn dust gives Aldehydes and Ketones without over-oxidation; H₂O₂ oxidizes aldehydes to acids
mechanismType: 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition to molozonide, rearrangement to ozonide, Zn reductive cleavage
keyRule: Cleaves C=C double bond cleanly to locate positions of double bonds in unknown structures.

chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques (GOC)
name: Reimer-Tiemann Reaction
keyRule: Intermediate electrophile is neutral singlet Dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂) possessing 6 valence electrons.
